items.title: Section: Cosmetics, Daily Routine, and the Widening Reach of Each Faculty — Reasons Four Through Six

items.zh: 又嚴飾差別所攝受故，次第宣說。諸受欲者，必以安繕那等先莊眉眼，次以耳璫、耳輪等莊嚴其耳，非於餘根。如是嚴飾，是第四因緣。又依作業、飲食、習欲等事，次第宣說。由諸眾生皆先依止身語二業若淨不淨方便勤求，次食段食；既飽醉已，習近諸欲。是第五因緣。又由作業差別攝受故，次第宣說。所以者何？由眼能見種種諸色；往還無失；威儀不亂；記識他身曾見不見及怨親中；了悟方所，宣示於他，起想言說；覩眾舞樂角力戲等，廣受種種世間喜樂，長養依身。如是等類，有無量種眼界作業。由耳能聞種種音聲，因此了悟善說、惡說種種義理，起諸言論；因聞種種微妙樂音，廣受種種世間喜樂，長養依身。如是等類耳界作業，比前狹劣。鼻界能嗅種種諸香，尋香而往，受諸喜樂，長養依身。如是等類鼻界作業，方前狹劣。舌界能甞種種諸味，受諸喜樂，長養依身。如是等類舌界作業，方前狹劣。身界能觸種種所觸，受諸喜樂，雖能長養依身，然彼樂具，或於一時復為損害。如是等類身界作業，最為狹劣。是名第六次第宣說因緣。於此眼等六種因緣差別中，意遍行故，最後宣說。為攝如是次第因緣，中嗢拕南曰：眾多、順世俗、喜樂、與莊嚴、隨二種作業，故次第宣說。復次，此十八界，當知能攝一切經中所說餘界。
items.en: Adornment likewise governs the sequence. Those given to pleasure invariably apply eye-shadow to the brows and eyes before hanging earrings and ear-ornaments on the ears, never on any other faculty — this adornment is the fourth reason. Ordinary activity, eating, and indulgence likewise govern the sequence: all beings first pursue wholesome or unwholesome bodily and verbal action to secure their needs, then eat their solid food, and only once fed and content do they turn to sensory indulgence — this is the fifth reason. Each faculty's own specific range of activity likewise governs the sequence. Why? Because the eye sees countless forms... this is the eye's limitless range of activity. Because the ear hears countless sounds... the ear's range, though still broad, is narrower than the eye's. The nose smells countless scents... narrower still than the ear's. The tongue tastes countless flavours... narrower still than the nose's. The body touches countless textures and receives pleasure from them, and though this nourishes the body it depends on, such pleasurable implements can sometimes cause harm instead — the body's range is the narrowest of all. This is the sixth reason for the sequence. Among these six faculty-based reasons, mind is named last because it operates pervasively throughout all of them. [Summary verse:] Abundance, conforming to worldly custom, pleasure and adornment, and the two kinds of activity — thus the sequence is taught. Moreover, these eighteen elements should be understood to subsume every other "element" spoken of anywhere in scripture.

items.title: Section: Two Hard Questions — Why Form-Realm Beings Still Have a Nose and Tongue, and Whether Thought Persists Above the Second Absorption

items.zh: 問：生色界者，已於境界而得離欲，何緣復生鼻、舌兩界？答：為令所依身端嚴故。又色界中，於此二種未離欲故。問：生第二靜慮或生上地，若有尋有伺眼等識現在前，云何此地無尋無伺？若不現前，云何於彼有色諸根而能領受彼地境界？答：由有尋有伺諸識種子隨逐無尋無伺三摩地故，從彼起已，此得現前。又此起已，識現行時，復為無尋無伺三摩地種子之所隨逐，是故此地非是一向無尋無伺。
items.en: Question: those born in the form realm have already become free of desire for those objects — why do the nose and tongue elements still arise for them? Answer: so that the body they depend on appears dignified and complete. Also, in the form realm, desire for these two faculties themselves has not yet been abandoned. Question: for those born in the second absorption or higher, if examination-and-reflection-accompanied eye-consciousness and the rest were present, how could this level be called free of examination and reflection? And if not present, how could their intact physical faculties still perceive that realm's objects? Answer: because seeds for examination-and-reflection-accompanied consciousness continue to accompany the examination-free stillness, such consciousness can become active again upon emerging from it; and once active, it is in turn accompanied by seeds for that examination-free stillness — hence this level is not absolutely, exclusively free of examination and reflection.

items.zh: 由彼有情於諸尋伺以性離欲而離欲故，彼地雖名無尋無伺，此復現行，亦無過失。

items.title: Section: Two Eyes, One Seeing — Closing the Hard Questions with the Lamp-Flame Analogy

items.zh: 問：何緣眼界、耳界、鼻界各生二分，非餘？答：為令依止得端嚴故。問：眼、耳與鼻諸識生時，為依二分，當言一耶？當言二耶？答：當言唯一。何以故？若彼一分無障不壞，識明了生；若彼有障，或復失壞，識不明了生故。又識非色故，無有如色由方所別成二分義。問：眼與眼識若是因果，云何俱有？若俱有者，云何得成因果兩性？答：識依眼生，非如種芽因果道理。何以故？眼與眼識，非正生因，唯建立因。是故此二俱時而有，因果性成。猶如燈焰光明道理。如眼與眼識。耳、鼻、舌、身與彼諸識，當知亦爾。若異此者，雖有自種，無所依故，眼等諸識應不得生。
items.en: Question: why do the eye, ear, and nose elements each generate two parts, and not the others? Answer: so that what they depend on appears dignified. Question: when eye, ear, and nose consciousness arise, depending on the two parts, should the consciousness be said to be one, or two? Answer: only one. Why? Because if that one part is unobstructed and undamaged, consciousness arises clearly; if obstructed or damaged, consciousness arises unclearly. And because consciousness is not form, it has no spatial location the way form does, and so no sense in which it splits into two parts as form does. Question: if the eye and eye-consciousness are cause and effect, how can they exist simultaneously? And if simultaneous, how can they be cause and effect at all? Answer: consciousness depends on the eye and arises, but not according to the seed-and-sprout kind of causality. Why? Because the eye and eye-consciousness are not a generating cause but only a supporting cause — hence the two exist simultaneously, and their causal nature is thereby established. It is like the principle of a flame and the light it gives off. As with the eye and eye-consciousness, so too should ear, nose, tongue, and body be understood with their own respective consciousnesses. Were it otherwise, though each consciousness has its own seed, lacking anything to depend on, the eye and other consciousnesses could not arise at all.

items.title: Section: Which Elements Definitely Arise in Which Realm — Desire, Form, and Formless

items.zh: 問：若於欲界或生或長，當言眼界決定轉耶？答：此非一向。如眼界，耳、鼻、舌界及彼識界，當知亦爾。身界決定轉。如是身識界，意界，法界，意識界，色、聲、香、味、觸界亦爾。問：若於色界或生或長，當言眼界決定轉耶？答：決定轉。如眼界，如是耳、鼻、舌、身界，眼、耳、身識界亦爾。除香、味界及彼識界，餘一切界亦決定轉。於無色界或生或長，除意界、法界、意識界，餘定不轉，唯除自在所獲諸色。當知三界於彼定轉。
items.en: Question: for one born or matured in the desire realm, does the eye element definitely arise? Answer: not necessarily. As with the eye element, so too should ear, nose, and tongue elements and their consciousnesses be understood. The body element definitely arises. So too do body-consciousness, mind, the dharma-element, mind-consciousness, and colour, sound, scent, taste, and touch. Question: for one born or matured in the form realm, does the eye element definitely arise? Answer: it definitely arises. As with the eye element, so too do ear, nose, tongue, and body elements, and eye-, ear-, and body-consciousness. Apart from scent, taste, and their consciousnesses, all remaining elements likewise definitely arise. For one born or matured in the formless realm, apart from mind, the dharma-element, and mind-consciousness, the rest definitely do not arise, save only form obtained through mastery of meditative absorption. These three elements should be understood to definitely arise there.

blocks.text: Why the senses are listed in this order, and two puzzles: why form-realm gods have noses and tongues, and whether two eyes make two seeings.

Beings first pursue bodily and verbal action, then eat, then indulge. The eye's reach is widest, then the ear's, then nose and tongue, and the body's narrowest. Mind is named last because it works with all the others.

Form-realm gods have nose and tongue so that the body appears dignified, and because desire for these has not yet been fully abandoned. Master Cháng Bǎi: absorption above the second meditation is not wholly free of thinking; on emerging, it may arise.
Consciousness does not occupy space, so it does not split into two. Master Cháng Bǎi: faculty and consciousness are simultaneous cause and effect by dominant condition.
Apart from these three, the rest do not arise, except form gained through meditative mastery.
"Consciousness does not occupy space." Two eyes, one seeing: the treatise uses ordinary experience to show that mind is not a thing among things.

quiz.q: How does the fifth reason, activity, eating, and indulgence, correspond to the objects?
options: body is smell, speech taste, food form and sound, indulgence mental objects, desire lying in mind
body is form, speech sound, solid food smell and taste, and indulgence touch
body is eye, speech ear, food body, indulgence mind
all five are form
quiz.why: The treatise says beings first pursue bodily and verbal action, then eat solid food, and only then indulge. Master Cháng Bǎi matches these to the sequence of objects: body is form, speech is sound, solid food is smell and taste, and indulgence is touch. The English "fed and content" softens 飽醉, full and intoxicated.

quiz.q: In the sixth reason, how do the five faculties' ranges compare?
options: the eye's is widest, ear, nose, and tongue narrowing, the body's narrowest
the body's is widest, narrowing through tongue, nose, and ear, the eye's narrowest, since the body covers all and eyes are two
all five are equal
the ear's is widest and the eye's narrowest
quiz.why: The treatise says the eye has limitless activity, the ear's is narrower, the nose's and tongue's narrower still, and the body's narrowest. Master Cháng Bǎi: the very things that give the body pleasure may at times harm it. This is one of six reasons, and much of the detail, abridged in the Chinese here, is missing from the English.

quiz.q: Why is the mental element named last, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: mind pervades eye through body and all objects, and with the five there is surely mind
mind matters least, placed last, the five being the focus of practice and mind negligible
mind exists only in the form realm
mind is an outsiders' term
quiz.why: The treatise says that among these six reasons mind is named last because it operates pervasively. Master Cháng Bǎi: mind is present with eye, ear, nose, tongue, and body, and so the mental element is named last; since mind pervades all objects, wherever the five faculties function, mind is surely there.

quiz.q: Why do those born in the form realm still have nose and tongue elements?
options: because they still eat and smell, gods needing solid food, so nose and tongue arise for enjoyment
through an error of karma
the form realm in fact has neither
so the body appears dignified, and desire for these two is not yet abandoned
quiz.why: The treatise answers that this is so the body appears dignified, and because desire for these two has not yet been abandoned in the form realm. Master Cháng Bǎi: form-realm gods have no solid food, and so no smell, taste, or nose- and tongue-consciousness. So the faculties remain though their objects do not.

quiz.q: In the second absorption and above, eye-consciousness has investigation. How is that level called free of it?
options: higher eye-consciousness has none at all, the question being hypothetical and needing no answer
it is not absolutely free, for investigation may arise on emerging; the level is defined by having no desire for investigation
there is no eye-consciousness above
investigation is form, unrelated to consciousness
quiz.why: The treatise concludes this level is not absolutely free of investigation. Master Cháng Bǎi: absorption from the second up is not wholly free of it, and on emerging it may arise; the definition of the level lies in having no desire for investigation, not in whether it is active. The sentence of the treatise giving this is missing from the English.

quiz.q: The English has "depending on one part or two? Answer: only one." Is this right?
options: right: consciousness depends on one eye only, the other being idle ornament, and the English fits exactly
reversed: the question is whether consciousness is one or two when it depends on both, and "one" means consciousness; the English has it depend on one part
reversed: the answer should be two eye-consciousnesses
the Chinese asks about ears, not eyes
quiz.why: The question is about consciousness: when it depends on both parts, is it one or two? One, because consciousness does not occupy space. Master Cháng Bǎi: it does not split into two as eyes occupy two sides; and the lecture elsewhere says a single eye-consciousness does arise in dependence on both eyes. The English makes "one" the count of parts relied on.

quiz.q: The English has "only a supporting cause" for 唯建立因. Why is this better than a literal rendering, and how are the eye and consciousness simultaneous yet cause and effect?
options: 建立因 is a direct cause like seed and sprout, the eye generating consciousness, so "supporting" is too weak and should be "generating"
建立因 is merit built by practice
建立因 is building a house
建立因 is the dominant condition, not the seed cause; like a flame and its light, simultaneous; "supporting" is clearer than "establishing"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: here they are simultaneous and cause and effect by way of dominant condition, not by seed or causal condition; the Mahāyāna holds both simultaneous and successive cause and effect. "Supporting cause" tells the reader what kind of cause this is, as "establishing cause" would not. This is a place where the English helps.

quiz.q: For one born or matured in the formless realm, what of the elements?
options: apart from form, sound, and touch, the rest definitely arise, the formless having subtle such things
all eighteen definitely arise
none of the eighteen arises
apart from mind, the phenomena-element, and mental consciousness, the rest definitely do not arise, save form gained through mastery
quiz.why: The treatise says that apart from these three, the rest definitely do not arise, save form gained through mastery. Master Cháng Bǎi: form born of mastery of absorption is a separate matter. The English "none of the rest definitely arise" reads as "not necessarily," whereas the Chinese says they definitely do not.
